part.text:
Set up the project:

- `index.js` — `toRegexRange(min, max, opts)` library. Converts a range into one regex, e.g. `1-100` → `(?:[1-9]|[1-9][0-9]|100)`. Supports negatives and `{ anchor, capture }` options.
- `bin/cli.js` — CLI: `range-to-regex 1-100`, `range-to-regex 1 100 --anchor`.
- `test/index.js` — self-contained tests (no deps).
- `package.json` — `main`, `bin`, `npm test`.

The algorithm splits the range by digit-width and merges aligned digit blocks. Node isn't installed in this environment, so I validated a line-by-line port with Python across all edge cases plus 3000 randomized ranges (including boundaries and leading-zero rejection) — all pass.

Run it with:
```
npm test
node bin/cli.js 1-100
```

Note: I could not execute `npm test`/lint here because no Node runtime is available.
